headline: Low interaction risk overall: no shared channels or writes are exposed, so prompt injection, leakage, and conflict pathways are largely blocked.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a docs-only content-writing repo with no I/O surfaces or runnable agent behavior; Profile B has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem, or MCP bridge. With no shared communication channel, there is no plausible default prompt-injection path between them.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, message queue, or filesystem bridge is added between the two profiles, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared copy-paste workflows.
Do not add MCP or queue-based handoff without provenance tagging.
Review any future integration for explicit instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile touches data classes, and B explicitly has no filesystem read, clipboard, screen capture, or network egress. A is a static repo listing with no runtime data path. There is no documented route for sensitive data to flow from A to B or out of B.
conditions: IF either profile is later granted filesystem read or network egress, leakage analysis must be revisited.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in any shared workspace.
Reassess if either agent begins handling PHI, credentials, or customer data.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no declared write, git, or network capabilities, and B explicitly cannot write the filesystem or modify git state. Because neither side can mutate a shared resource, there is no capability overlap that can create write conflicts.
conditions: IF A gains write or git capabilities, or B is reconfigured to write shared state, conflict risk may emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in shared environments.
Do not mount a common writable workspace.
Add locking only if future write capabilities are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a content-writing repo that could supply text, but B is a data orchestrator with no stdin/stdout, files, or API calls exposed here, so there is no default automated handoff. Any cascade would require an unusual external wrapper that treats A's output as authoritative.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator pipes A's text into B without validation, cascading error risk increases.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any handoff.
Require schema validation on A's outputs.
Do not auto-execute actions from generated text.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes are touched by either profile, and neither profile declares residency, retention, or regulated-data handling. With no identified regulated data flow, there is no compliance mismatch to assess between A and B.
conditions: IF either profile begins processing regulated data or declares residency/retention constraints, compliance must be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Add retention and residency metadata if regulated data is introduced.
